items.coder_A: uncertain: BG chemosensitiser could be enabling rather than candidate
items.reason: O6-benzylguanine 'selectively and irreversibly inactivates the DNA-repair enzyme, O6- alkylguanine DNA-alkyltransferase' to potentiate temozolomide/carmustine in the tumour; R6 makes such a chemosensitiser a candidate in its own right.
BG is the only investigational pharmacological agent; temozolomide/carmustine are established therapies and the P140K-MGMT cells are an excluded gene-modified cell product, so rule 4 applies.

items.proposed: MGMT eligibility, candidate_matched true, matched_agent o6-benzylguanine
items.reason: 'Participant must have unmethylated MGMT' is an entry requirement, and R6 states the MGMT match counts for an MGMT-targeting candidate such as O6-benzylguanine.

combination_partners records antitumour therapy in the experimental arm; the P140K-MGMT cells are given to 'protect hematopoiesis', not as antitumour therapy, so they are not a partner (they remain listed as an excluded_intervention_type agent).

note: Positive candidate_matched_selection (MGMT + BG via R6), so it goes to D21 human review. Carmustine role (priority 3) differs between coders: established_therapy_experiment (A) vs soc_backbone (B); either way not a candidate. 'O6-benzylguanine' has no INN in the record and is kept as written.
